alice.w: Quick question — we just merged #4921 which tweaks the default request timeout from 30s -> 35s for the serving runtime. Is that a patch or a minor bump?
ben.k: If it's purely internal default tuning with no public API change, leaning patch.
carol: Agree. The rule we've followed: patch for bugfixes and internal defaults, minor if we change public SDK behavior/contract.
dave: One edge: if customers rely on default for SLA calculations, that could be considered behavior change. Any telemetry showing customers impacted?
emily: No alerts in the last 90 days. This was to reduce spurious timeouts in our test fleet.
alice.w: OK. Want to capture an explicit guideline so release engineers and deploy-bot tagging are consistent.
ben.k: Proposal (short):
```
- bump PATCH for internal tuning, config defaults, non-breaking perf tweaks
- bump MINOR for any change that alters observable API semantics, default return shapes, or SDK-facing defaults
- bump MAJOR for breaking changes
```
carol: +1. Also: if a change requires post-deploy customer opt-in or migration steps, treat as minor at least.
dave: How about tagging and PR title conventions? I keep seeing inconsistent tags like `chore:` vs `fix:`. That matters for automated release notes.
emily: Suggestion: PR labels map to bump type: `fix/patch`, `feat/minor`, `breaking/major`. Release tooling can infer semver from labels.
alice.w: Can deploy-bot respect labels so we get `v1.2.3` vs `v1.3.0` automatically?
deploy-bot: @alice.w I can if releases are created via the release workflow. Add a `semver:patch` or `semver:minor` label and run `/release create` or tag a release branch. I will then create an annotated tag: `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`.
ben.k: Also add a human-in-the-loop step for ambiguous cases — checklist item in the release PR for release owner to confirm.
carol: For hotfixes that were cherry-picked into an older maintenance branch, we should add a `cherry` footer in the changelog entry and tag both branches separately.
dave: Any objections to this short playbook being added to our release docs?
emily: No objections. I'll draft a one-page in docs/releases and include a TL;DR table mapping label->bump.
alice.w: One more operational detail: rollback policy. If a patch causes regression we prefer rollback to the previous patch on the same minor line, right?
ben.k: Yes — rollback to previous patch when regression is severe. If regression is subtle and we need feature rollback, we might cut a patch that reverts only the bad commit and release quickly.
carol: Note: add a line about release notes granularity — patch notes should still include short rationale and revert instructions. Keeps oncall sane.
dave: Can deploy-bot post a standard footer in the release PR with the tag command it used and a rollback command like `git revert -m 1 <merge-commit> && git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "revert"`?
deploy-bot: I can append a standard snippet to the release PR and to the rollout Slack thread after deploy: `Rollback: git revert <merge-commit> && git push && /release create vX.Y.Z` (human confirmation required).
emily: Awesome. I'll add examples to the doc: how to tag, sample changelog entry, and the label matrix.
alice.w: OK let's ship the doc and follow the label mapping for this change. I'll relabel #4921 to `semver:patch`. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
ben.k: :thumbsup:
carol: Thanks — makes the next release easier.
deploy-bot: Deploy started to staging (staging-2027-03-05-09:12) — reporting back on success/failure.
dave: staging passed for the small canary. planning prod push in the 13:00 change window.
emily: Drafted the doc PR at https://git.internal/redwood/releases/playbook (will link here).
